stem: The museum exhibit perplexing mixed significant cultural artifacts with gaudy trinkets, leading one critic to suggest that the exhibit’s curator could not distinguish the important pieces from those that were ____.
It was (i)____ the candidate’s insistence that there will be completely disclosure that she (ii)____ probing questions from reporters.

Critics of the company’s senior management will be (i)____ by Han’s careful and meticulous account of its actions. Despite the book’s (ii)____ title, the author has no designs on scandal; in fact, if anything, her account tends toward (iii)____, applauding the company’s all-conquering success without reservation.

The scholars’ hypothesis challenges the scope of human psychological and behavioral universal, but does not dispense with them entirely: the team remains confident that displays of pride, for instance, are ____.

As some primate experts have argued, the finding that related species have similar social structures, presumably as a result of shared genes inherited from a common ancestor, ____ nongenetic explanations of social behavior.

While spectroscopy may be an obscure tool, there is nothing correspondingly ____ about claims concerning its importance: it proved that the rest of the universe is built form the same kinds of atoms as we are.

The legislators didn’t merely sell out to business; they retreated to ____ style of governing whereby the interest group that is currently lobbying the hardest on an issue determines the party’s position.
